observations.attribute: serpentine tubular structure in right medial lung zone
observations.value: a well-defined, continuous, branching tubular opacity coursing vertically through the right mid-lung field, with caliber change and meandering course; appears vascular rather than air-filled (no air bronchograms within it)

left lung is smaller in volume, mediastinum shifted leftward, left hemidiaphragm elevated, left intercostal spaces narrowed — consistent with chronic volume loss (e.g., fibrosis, atelectasis, or prior surgery)
mediastinum displaced toward the left hemithorax; cardiac silhouette and trachea deviated left
not dilated; no evidence of bronchiectasis or chronic infection in right lung fields
no visible pleural line or absence of lung markings peripherally on either side; lung edges intact
aortic knob visible on left side of mediastinum; no right-sided arch contour
no focal saccular or fusiform dilation of pulmonary arteries; tubular structure follows venous rather than arterial course (drains toward left atrium region)
bronchial arteries are typically too small to be visible on plain CXR; no hypertrophic collateral vessels seen

hypotheses.name: Anomalous systemic-to-pulmonary venous connection (e.g., scimitar syndrome variant or single meandering pulmonary vein)
hypotheses.basis: Serpentine tubular structure matches expected appearance of anomalous pulmonary vein draining into IVC or right atrium; left volume loss may reflect hypoplasia or sequestration associated with anomalous drainage

hypotheses.basis: Meandering course and size suggest a large vein; location in medial right lung aligns with possible anomalous right middle lobe vein; left volume loss may be unrelated or secondary to compensatory hyperinflation
